Develop, build, and deploy

|View as Markdown|Agent setup

cf develops, builds, and deploys Workers projects with the same CLI that manages the rest of your Cloudflare account. To create a project, follow Deploy your first Worker.

Configure the project with cloudflare.config.ts. Builds write Build Output to .cloudflare/output/v1/.

How cf runs your project

cf does not run a dev server or bundler itself. For cf dev, cf build, and every other command that builds first, cf hands the work to one of these tools:

  1. The framework's own command. When cf detects a supported framework, it runs that framework's dev or build command with the executable installed in your project, including a dependency hoisted to the workspace root. In a Vite or Vite+ project, including a project created with cf init, that is vite or vp.
  2. An installed Cloudflare build tool. Otherwise, cf uses the Cloudflare build tool listed in the project's package.json dependencies: the Cloudflare Vite plugin, or Wrangler when the Vite plugin is not listed.

cf supports the latest release of the Cloudflare Vite plugin 2.0 and the latest release of Wrangler. The Vite plugin 2.0 does not depend on Wrangler.

Wrangler builds projects such as those that cf migrate converts with the Wrangler bundler, and static sites that automatic configuration sets up. These projects keep build settings, such as the static assets directory, in a generated wrangler.config.ts file. That file is experimental and can change.

cf build and cf deploy run the framework's own build command, such as vite build or astro build, not the build script in package.json. If your build script runs extra steps, such as tsc -b && vite build, chain those steps with cf build in your own script instead:

cf dev forwards extra arguments to the selected development server. This applies to framework commands and installed Cloudflare build tools. To set the port and host in a Vite project, run:

Use -- to separate server arguments from cf options:

Supported arguments depend on the selected development server. The server rejects arguments it does not support, even after --.

cf build accepts only --mode. For framework support for --mode, refer to Modes.

Automatic configuration

When a project has no cloudflare.config.ts, cf tries to detect its framework and set the project up for Cloudflare before it continues. This automatic configuration runs from these commands:

  • cf dev and cf build
  • cf deploy, including cf deploy --dry-run
  • cf previews deploy
  • cf workers versions create, cf workers triggers deploy, and cf workers check
  • cf init

A project counts as configured only when cloudflare.config.ts exists in the directory where you run the command. Passing --prebuilt skips automatic configuration.

In a terminal, cf shows the planned changes and asks before it applies them. Without a terminal, or in CI, it applies the changes and installs packages without asking. Run cf init . locally before you set up CI. It configures an existing project without building it. Review the changes and commit them. For the list of changes, refer to Start from an existing project.

Wrangler projects

Automatic configuration does not read Wrangler configuration files. In a project that has wrangler.jsonc, wrangler.json, or wrangler.toml but no cloudflare.config.ts, do not run cf init ., cf dev, cf build, cf deploy, or another command that builds.

In a framework or static-assets project, cf writes a new cloudflare.config.ts that ignores the Wrangler configuration, including its entrypoint and bindings. In a Worker project without a detected framework, the command fails with an error such as cloudflare.config.ts is required when --experimental-new-config is enabled. Convert the project with cf migrate first. Refer to Migrate a Wrangler project.

Start development

Start the project's development server:

The dev server prints its local URL. Append /cdn-cgi/local/explorer to that URL to open Local Explorer. Use it to inspect local binding data, view logs and traces, and test Cron Triggers with a chosen cron expression and scheduled time.

Local variables and secrets

During cf dev, the development server reads values for your Worker's variables and secrets from files in the project directory. When you pass --mode, it also reads the files for that mode.

The Cloudflare Vite plugin reads both of these groups:

  • .env, .env.local, .env.<MODE>, and .env.<MODE>.local, in that order. A value in a later file overrides the same variable in an earlier one.
  • .dev.vars.<MODE> if it exists, otherwise .dev.vars.

Wrangler reads .dev.vars.<MODE> if it exists, otherwise .dev.vars. It reads the .env files only when the project has no .dev.vars file.

cf also reads its own credentials, such as CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN, from the same .env files. For details, refer to Load credentials from a .env file.

Build

Build the project:

After the build finishes, cf reads and validates .cloudflare/output/v1/. cf build does not upload anything and does not need credentials.

Deploy

cf deploy builds the project, validates Build Output, resolves your credentials and account, uploads a new Worker Version, and deploys it:

Sign in with cf auth login, or set CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN, before you deploy. For details, refer to Sign in.

cf deploy can provision missing resources for bindings that omit resource identifiers. It does not write provisioned identifiers back to cloudflare.config.ts. To make those bindings fail instead, pass --no-provision.

cf deploy accepts these options:

Option Purpose
--dry-run Builds and validates the Worker without uploading it
--message <TEXT> Records a message on the Worker Version
--tag <TAG> Records a tag on the Worker Version
--secrets-file <PATH> Uploads secrets from a JSON or .env format file with the version
--dispatch-namespace <NAMESPACE> Deploys a Workers for Platforms user Worker to that dispatch namespace
--containers-rollout <STRATEGY> Sets the Container rollout strategy: immediate, gradual, or none
--worker <NAME> Selects a Worker from Build Output instead of the default Worker
--prebuilt Deploys existing Build Output without building
--no-provision Fails on bindings without resource identifiers instead of creating resources
--force Uploads in CI even when the remote Worker has changes that conflict with the local Build Output

--dry-run sends no API requests and needs no credentials, so you can validate a project before you sign in. In a project without cloudflare.config.ts, it still runs automatic configuration first, which can install packages and change files.

Deploy a static assets directory

To deploy a directory of files that another tool already built, such as a static site, pass the directory:

cf skips the build and deploys the files as an assets-only Worker. When the project has a cloudflare.config.ts, cf uses its Worker settings, such as the name. Otherwise, it names the Worker after the name in package.json, or after the project directory. cf previews deploy and cf workers versions create accept a directory in the same way.

Use this form only for projects without server-side code. When cloudflare.config.ts configures a Worker entrypoint or Containers, the command fails. Run it without the directory so that cf builds the project. You cannot combine a directory with --prebuilt or --worker.

Modes

A mode selects which configuration a function-form cloudflare.config.ts returns. Pass it with --mode or -m:

When you omit --mode, the Cloudflare Vite plugin uses development for cf dev and production for builds. Builds through Wrangler and API commands leave the mode undefined. For the full list, refer to Select a mode.

When cf runs a framework's own command, only Vite and Astro accept --mode. Other framework commands fail with an error. Refer to A framework rejects --mode.

This configuration deploys a separate staging Worker with its own API origin:

Return one complete configuration for each mode. Programmatic configuration does not merge environment blocks the way Wrangler environments do. A mode deploys a separate Worker only when it returns a different name.

Build Output records the mode it was built with. When you deploy an existing build, pass the same mode.

Deploy a prebuilt build

Pass --prebuilt to deploy an existing .cloudflare/output/v1/ directory without building. One CI job can build, and another can deploy the restored directory. --prebuilt also skips automatic configuration.

The deploy command must request the mode that Build Output records:

  • When Build Output records a mode, pass exactly that mode with --mode.
  • When Build Output records no mode, do not pass --mode.

Vite builds always record a mode. cf build without --mode records production, so deploy that build with --mode production:

Deploy a staging build with the staging mode:

Builds through Wrangler record a mode only when you pass --mode to cf build. To check the recorded mode, read buildContext.mode in .cloudflare/output/v1/config.json.

The same rule applies to --prebuilt with cf previews deploy, cf workers versions create, cf workers triggers deploy, and cf workers check. When the modes do not match, the command stops before it uploads anything and prints the --mode value to use.

For a complete pipeline, refer to Use cf in CI.

Upload a version

Upload a Worker Version without deploying it:

This command builds and validates the project the same way as cf deploy. It accepts --prebuilt, --mode, --message, --tag, --secrets-file, --dry-run, and --worker. Use --preview-alias <ALIAS> to give the version a preview URL alias.

To send traffic to an uploaded version, create a deployment:

Deploy triggers

Apply trigger configuration from Build Output without uploading a new version:

This command applies routes, custom domains, the workers.dev setting, cron schedules, Queue consumers, and Workflows. It builds the project unless you pass --prebuilt. It also accepts --mode, --worker, and --dry-run. A dry run sends no API requests.

Deploy a preview

Deploy the project as a Worker Preview:

The command builds the project with isPreview set to true, so a function-form cloudflare.config.ts can return preview-specific settings. It then uploads the preview and prints the result as JSON.

The preview name defaults to the current branch. cf reads the branch from Workers Builds, GitHub Actions, or GitLab CI/CD, and then from Git. To override the branch name, pass --preview-name. This flag is required on a detached HEAD with no CI branch:

The command accepts --mode, --worker, and --prebuilt. With --prebuilt, Build Output must come from a preview build, and the mode rule applies. --dry-run checks the arguments and shows what the command would run, without building or uploading.

The JSON result contains type, version, preview_id, preview_name, preview_slug, preview_urls, deployment_id, and deployment_urls.

Previews do not support Durable Object-managed Containers. cf deploy, cf workers versions create, and cf workers triggers deploy refuse preview Build Output and print the cf previews deploy command to use instead.

Profile Worker startup

Profile the Worker's startup performance locally:

The command builds the project unless you pass --prebuilt. It prints the bundle size and startup timings as JSON, and writes a CPU profile to worker-startup.cpuprofile. Use --outfile <PATH> to choose a different file. The command also accepts --mode and --worker.

The measurement runs on your machine. Use it to find where startup time goes, not to predict startup time on Cloudflare.

Generate types

Generate TypeScript types from cloudflare.config.ts:

The command writes .cloudflare/types/index.d.ts, which contains the Env binding types and the Workers runtime types. Pass --no-include-runtime to leave out the runtime types, or --mode to evaluate the configuration for a named mode.

The Cloudflare Vite plugin writes the same file during development and builds. Run cf workers types in projects that build through Wrangler, or before a type check. Projects created with cf init include a typecheck script that runs cf workers types and then the Vite+ type check.

Local resource data

Add --local to a supported command to run it against a local simulation instead of the Cloudflare API:

--local works only for a few resources that local development provides. cf starts a short-lived local runtime for each command, so no dev server needs to be running. Local support covers these commands:

  • cf kv keys get, cf kv keys list, cf kv keys put, and cf kv keys delete
  • cf kv bulk get, cf kv bulk put, and cf kv bulk delete
  • cf d1 raw
  • cf d1 migrations list and cf d1 migrations apply
  • cf r2 objects get, cf r2 objects put, cf r2 objects list, and cf r2 objects bulk-delete
  • cf flagship apps flags list, get, create, update, patch, delete, and evaluate
  • cf flagship apps evaluate get
  • cf d1 list, cf kv namespaces list, cf flagship apps list, and cf r2 buckets list

cf d1 query has no local equivalent. Use cf d1 raw instead. A command without a local equivalent fails with This command has no local equivalent. instead of calling the Cloudflare API.

By default, --local keeps its data in .cloudflare/state/v3 next to the nearest cloudflare.config.ts. The Cloudflare Vite plugin 2.0 uses the same directory, so a command such as cf kv keys list --local reads the data your development server created. Pass --persist-to <DIRECTORY> to use <DIRECTORY>/v3 instead. Outside a project, --local needs --persist-to. --persist-to works only with --local.

Which configuration each command reads

Project commands, such as cf dev, cf build, and cf deploy, run a build tool that loads the whole cloudflare.config.ts, including the Worker and Containers.

Ordinary API commands, such as cf d1 list, read only accountId and complianceRegion from the nearest cloudflare.config.ts in the current directory or a parent directory. A syntax error, import error, or top-level runtime error in that file still stops them. For details, refer to Set account defaults.

API credentials, such as CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN, can also come from a .env file in the current directory. Commands that build first, such as cf deploy, load those values after the build finishes. For details, refer to Load credentials from a .env file.

Troubleshooting

No dev server is installed

cf found no framework that it recognizes and no Cloudflare build tool declared in package.json, for example in an empty directory. To create a project, run cf init.

Dependencies are not installed

In a configured project whose dependencies are not installed, Vite reports that it cannot resolve @cloudflare/vite-plugin, or cf reports that a build tool is declared but not installed. Install dependencies with your package manager, then run the command again.

Arguments are rejected

Check which development server cf dev selects and which arguments it supports. If a server argument conflicts with a cf option, pass it after --. The selected server still rejects unsupported arguments and invalid values.

A framework rejects --mode

Only Vite and Astro accept --mode when cf runs a framework command. Run the command without --mode.

A prebuilt deploy rejects the mode

Pass exactly the mode that Build Output records, or omit --mode when it records none. Refer to Deploy a prebuilt build.

Build Output is missing

A --prebuilt command found no build. Run cf build first, or restore the complete .cloudflare/output/v1/ directory from your build job. If the build job ran a beta release of cf, rebuild with the current release.

Preview output reaches a production deploy

The existing Build Output came from cf previews deploy. Run the suggested command to deploy the preview, or run cf build to create production output.

The preview name cannot be determined

cf previews deploy found no branch name, for example on a detached HEAD. Pass a name with --preview-name:

A local command has no local equivalent

The command does not support --local. For D1 queries, use cf d1 raw instead of cf d1 query. Otherwise, run the command without --local.
